concepts.title: Five-Phase Power Consolidation Architecture: The Sequential Lock
concepts.excerpt: Imagine a person who comes to power with no mandate. The system around them—the military, the oligarchy, the media, the institutions—was not built by them and is not controlled by them.

concepts.title: Institutional Trauma Lock: When Institutions Become Incapable of Resisting
concepts.excerpt: Imagine an institution—a military, a security service, a bureaucracy—that has been captured through loyalty testing.

concepts.title: Visibility Minimization as Power-Accumulation Strategy: The Invisibility Advantage
concepts.excerpt: Imagine a person in a system where power is distributed—oligarchs have independent wealth, the military has institutional autonomy, the media operates with some editorial freedom, institutions have their own norms and decision-making processes.

concepts.title: Plausible Deniability as Essential Escalation Framework: The Permission Structure for Violation
concepts.excerpt: Imagine a regime that wants to escalate violations—suppress opposition, violate constitutional limits, seize oligarchs' wealth, eliminate political rivals, conduct military operations without parliamentary approval.

concepts.title: Authority Testing as Loyalty Verification: Obedience as Complicity Lock
concepts.excerpt: A regime orders compliance with something manifestly unjust. The order contradicts law, morality, professional ethics, or personal conscience.

concepts.title: Institutional Capture Through Loyalty Networks: Replacing Independent Function With Regime Alignment
concepts.excerpt: An institution nominally has a function—courts dispense justice, media report information, military protects borders, bureaucracy administers law.

concepts.title: Media Capture and Trolling: Weaponizing Information Systems for Narrative Dominance
concepts.excerpt: Media capture serves two simultaneous functions. The first function is narrative control—the regime controls what information reaches the population and how that information is framed.

concepts.title: Pride as Epistemic Foundation: Making Belief Impervious to Evidence
concepts.excerpt: A regime wants people to believe certain things: "Our nation is strong," "Our leader is wise," "Our enemies are evil."

concepts.title: "People Want to Believe" Communication Strategy: Manufacturing Consent Through Desire
concepts.excerpt: People do not inhabit a world of pure facts. People inhabit a world of narratives—stories about what is true, what is good, what is possible.

concepts.title: Trolling the Press as Discourse Rejection: Making Journalism Itself the Enemy
concepts.excerpt: Normally, regimes battle journalists over specific claims. Did X happen?

concepts.title: Dependence-Based Ownership: Creating Permanent Debt Through Resource Control
concepts.excerpt: A regime creates situation where citizens are dependent on the regime for survival or welfare.

concepts.title: Economic Competence as Justification for Ruthlessness: Effectiveness as Moral Permission
concepts.excerpt: A regime violates constitutional limits. Citizens notice the contradiction immediately: the leadership operates outside legal constraint, suppresses opposition, controls courts.

concepts.title: The Law is Universal; Enforcement is Political: Selective Enforcement of Legitimate Laws
concepts.excerpt: The technique of applying laws that technically exist but are applied selectively to eliminate enemies.

concepts.title: The Pivot from Reactive to Ruthlessness: When Constraint Disappears
concepts.excerpt: A person navigating a system with distributed power begins by being reactive.

concepts.title: Consistency as Relative Advantage: Winning by Predictability While Others Adapt
concepts.excerpt: Imagine two actors in a conflict. One has a clear objective and pursues it relentlessly, adjusting tactics as needed but never changing the objective.

concepts.title: Hard-Then-Soft Baseline Shift: Resetting Expectations Through Escalation and De-escalation
concepts.excerpt: A system operates with certain expectations. Citizens expect that the government will permit some level of opposition.

concepts.title: Collect Everything Forever and Use Nothing Today: Deferred Leverage Intelligence Architecture
concepts.excerpt: A leader collects information on everyone—financial records, security files, compromising material.

concepts.title: Knowledge Asymmetry as Foundation of State Control: Making Uncertainty Unnavigable
concepts.excerpt: A population under state control operates with a fundamental disadvantage: they do not know what the state knows.

concepts.title: Information Asymmetry and Intelligence Dominance
concepts.excerpt: Greene identifies a principle that runs through multiple strategies (18: Use Spies; 19: Negotiate While Seeming Not to Negotiate; 26: Use Diplomatic Channels): win through knowing more than your opponent, not through raw power.

concepts.title: Information Control and Opacity Networks
concepts.excerpt: In any organization, the person who receives information first has advantage.

concepts.title: Generational Redemption Narrative: Making Youth Regime Supporters Through Meaning-Making
concepts.excerpt: A nation experienced profound humiliation. A generation suffered defeat.

concepts.title: Post-Ideological Nationalism: Power Without Philosophy
concepts.excerpt: Cold War regimes justified power through ideology. Soviet power was justified through Marxist-Leninist theory: the dictatorship of the proletariat, historical materialism, the inevitability of communist future.

concepts.title: Chilling Effect Through Plausible Deniable Assassination: Murdering Without Admission
concepts.excerpt: An opposition leader dies. A critical journalist dies. A potential rival dies.

concepts.title: Weaponized Transformation: The "Glow Up" as Strategic Power Signaling
concepts.excerpt: A person changes their physical presentation—loses weight, gains muscle, changes hairstyle, updates wardrobe.
